EventDetail:
AR Nagori National Art Competition 2.0

Guidelines

Theme: عزم و عمل (Azm-o-Amal)

 

Azm-o-Amal is the quiet strength behind every meaningful change. It lives in the streets we walk, the identities we shape, the futures we imagine, and the courage to act despite uncertainty. This theme invites young artists to transform resolve into visual expression capturing hope, responsibility, inclusion, and the belief that purposeful action, however small, can shape a better tomorrow.

 

عزم و عمل وہ خاموش طاقت ہے جو ہر مثبت تبدیلی کے پیچھے کارفرما ہوتی ہے۔ یہ ہمارے شہروں، ہمارے سماج، ہماری پہچان اور ہمارے خوابوں میں سانس لیتی ہے۔ یہ موضوع نوجوان فنکاروں کو دعوت دیتا ہے کہ وہ اپنے عزم، امید، شمولیت اور با معنی کوششوں کو بصری اظہار میں ڈھالیں—کیونکہ ہر سچا عمل ایک بہتر کل کی بنیاد رکھتا ہے۔

 

Participants are encouraged to interpret the theme through their own lived experiences and perspectives. The intent is not to limit expression, but to allow artists the freedom to reflect on personal, social, and collective narratives rooted in determination and action.

 

Who Can Participate?

  • Students currently enrolled in:
    • Matric
    • Intermediate
    • O Level
    • A Level
  • Open to students across Pakistan
  • Age group: approximately 15–19 years

 

Mediums

Acceptable mediums include:

  • Painting
  • Drawing
  • Mixed Media

Digitally manipulated or AI-generated artworks are not allowed.

 

Submission Format

  • Artwork must be photographed or scanned clearly
  • Submit via email (details to be shared separately)
  • Each submission must include:
    • The artwork image
    • A maximum 150-word description/artist statement explaining the concept and its link to the theme
  • Artist statement may be written in any regional language

 

Originality

  • All artworks must be original
  • Artworks must be created specifically for this competition
  • Previously exhibited or submitted works will not be accepted

 

Shortlisting & Final Display

  • Shortlisted participants will be informed via email
  • Shortlisted artists must submit their original artwork (hard copy) via courier to the Aga Khan University Institute for Educational Development which will be returned at the culmination of the contest.
  • Selected artworks will be displayed in a physical art exhibition
  • Final evaluation will be conducted by a jury panel

 

Important Dates

  • Submission Deadline: 20th, February 2026
  • Prize Distribution Ceremony: April 2026
  • Venue: Karachi
Title: A.R. Nagori Art Competition 2026 - Azm-o-Amal

Learning Objectives

By the end of this session, participants will be able to:

• Demonstrate how simulation design influences clinical reasoning and diagnostic decision-making
• Critically reflect on the use of virtual patients and major incident simulations to support reasoning and interdisciplinary learning
• Evaluate the role of generative AI in enhancing reflective practice within simulation-based education
• Apply transferable principles to strengthen clinical reasoning within their own educational contexts

About the Presenter

Dr Shazia Iqbal is a senior medical educator and clinician with extensive international experience in simulation-based medical education, clinical reasoning enhancement, and the ethical integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into health professions education. She is a Senior Fellow of the Higher Education Academy (SFHEA) and currently holds a senior faculty leadership role at the University of Buckingham, UK.

With a long-standing academic and clinical career spanning the UK and the Middle East, Dr Shazia has led and implemented large-scale simulation initiatives aimed at strengthening diagnostic reasoning, decision-making, and interdisciplinary teamwork. Her work includes the design and delivery of technology-enhanced clinical scenarios that bridge theory with authentic clinical practice.
Dr Shazia’s scholarly interests lie at the intersection of clinical simulation, generative AI, inquiry-based learning, and digital innovation, with a strong focus on ensuring that emerging technologies support rather than replace human judgement and professional reasoning. She is an international speaker, curriculum developer, and reviewer for leading medical education journals, and is recognised for translating educational research into meaningful, practice-based innovations.

Workshop Overview:

Rapidly identifying and managing life-threatening conditions with focused ultrasound is vital in emergency and critical care. This hands-on, full-day workshop equips you with the skills to master Point-of-Care Ultrasound (PoCUS) and make life-saving decisions.

Through a combination of interactive presentations, hands-on sessions, and case-based discussions, this workshop provides a unique and practical approach to skill development.

Who Should Attend?
Adult and pediatric physicians, working in Emergency, ICU, and Acute Medicine. 
Students and interns are not eligible to attend.

Workshop Modules
  • Basic orientation of ultrasound machine (Knobology and Image interpretation)
  • Approach to a patient with undifferentiated shock (inferior vena cava assessment, abdominal aortic aneurysm, intraabdominal free fluid, cardiac tamponade, left ventricular dysfunction, & massive pulmonary embolism)
  • Approach to a patient with respiratory failure (tension pneumothorax, pulmonary edema, pleural effusion, & pneumonia)
  • Role of PoCUS in cardiac arrest (cardiac standstill, pseudo PEA, & PoCUS pulse check)
  • Learning to perform ultrasound-guided central venous catheter (CVC) insertion

Learning Outcomes
  • Understand the basic knobology and ultrasound image interpretation
  • Apply PoCUS to rapidly assess patients with undifferentiated shock (cardiogenic shock, septic shock, hypovolemic and obstructive shock)
  • Acquire the skills to use PoCUS in the assessment of patients with undifferentiated respiratory failure (Pneumothorax, Pleural effusion, Pulmonary edema, & Pneumonia)
  • Gain confidence in utilizing PoCUS as a valuable diagnostic tool in cardiac arrest (H's and T's and PoCUS Pulse Check)
  • Learn to perform ultrasound-guided Central Venous Catheter (CVC) insertion

Workshop Director
  • Dr Noman Ali, Assistant Professor & Consultant, Department of Emergency Medicine, AKUH

Consultants, Department of Emergency Medicine, AKUH:
  • Dr Madiha Ismail
  • Dr Tanveer Tajuddin
  • Dr Rabia Hassan
  • Dr Hiba Kausar
  • Dr Noman Ali

EventDetail:
In this lecture, Glaire Anderson will be discussing her work, which bridges video games, GLAM (Galleries, Libraries, Archives, Museums) and academic sectors. She will discuss how her recent experiences as a games industry consultant and collaborator, as a speaker at #GDC2024 and as an academic game developer and entrepreneur engages with ongoing debates about historical and cultural representations in games, and the positive social impact of games.

Dr. Glaire Anderson is Senior Lecturer in Islamic Art in the School of History of Art at the University of Edinburgh and Founding Director and Principal Consultant of the Digital Lab for Islamic Visual Culture & Collections. Her second book A Bridge to the Sky: The Arts of Science in the Age of Abbas Ibn Firnas (Oxford University Press, 2024) examines early Islamic science and visual culture through the career of a 9th c. Cordoban intellectual remembered today for an early aeronautics experiment. Applying immersive 3D digital technologies to the work of Islamic art and architectural history is a longstanding focus of Anderson's research, and she was an external historian and art/architecture historian on Ubisoft's Assassin’s Creed Mirage and its ‘History of Baghdad’ educational Codex feature (Ubisoft Bordeaux, 2023).

This event will be held at the Aga Khan Centre - London and will also be streamed live via Zoom.

EventDetail:
The 7th Pulse Conference addresses the critical challenge of Sudden Cardiac Death (SCD). Organized by the Department of Cardiology and the Cardiac Sciences Collaboration, this year's theme, "Myths, Facts & Beyond," aims to bridge the gap between epidemiology, pathophysiology, and practical management. The conference features comprehensive sessions on prevention in the young, risk stratification in cardiomyopathies, and advanced therapeutic approaches, including public access defibrillation and AI in risk prediction.

• Event Objectives

1. To understand the epidemiology and pathophysiology of SCD in South Asia.
2. To discuss risk stratification, genetic testing, and imaging markers in cardiomyopathies.
3. To review therapeutic strategies including ICDs, VT ablation, and sympathetic denervation.
4. To explore the role of public health initiatives (CPR/AED) and future technologies (AI/Genomics).

• Moderator/s / Course Directors / Session Leadership

1. Conference Chair: Dr. Yawer Saeed
2. Section Head Cardiology: Dr. Osman Faheem
3. Session Chairs: Dr. Zainab Samad, Dr. Azam Shafquat, Dr. Amber Ashraf, Dr. Sohail Aziz, Dr. Ghazala Irfan, Dr. Azmat Hayat, Dr. Saulat Fatimi, Dr. Sohail Abrar, Dr. Khalida Soomro, Dr. Jack Rickard.

• Speakers and Topics

1. Keynote/International: Prof. Arshad Jahangir (Wake Forest), Dr. Jack Rickard (Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi), Dr. Umer Darr (Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi), Prof. Fu Siong Ng (Imperial College London), Dr. Rizwan Ali Muhammad (Albany Medical).
2. National/Regional: Dr. Faisal Qadir, Dr. Zainab Samad, Dr. Sohail Abrar, Dr. Fateh Ali Tipoo, Dr. Salman Kirmani, Dr. Abdul Mannan, Dr. Noor Baig, Prof. Abdul Hakeem, Dr. Fariha Sadiq Ali, Dr. Muhammad Tariq, Dr. Saleem Islam, Prof. Liaquat Zaman, Dr. Fawad Farooq.

• Who should attend: Cardiologists, Cardiothoracic Surgeons, Electrophysiologists, Residents, Fellows, Medical Students, General Practitioners, Emergency Medicine Physicians, and Allied Health Professionals.

• Topics/Highlights:

1. Pre-Conference Workshops (e.g., Cardio-Obstetrics, Watchman, Coronary Angiography, POCUS, Rotational Atherectomy).
2. SCD in the Young & Athletes.
3. Risk Stratification in Cardiomyopathies (Genetics, Imaging, EPS).
4. Therapeutic Approaches (ICD, CRT-D, VT Ablation, Cardiac Denervation).
5. Public Health: CPR/AED Programs & Ambulance Services.
6. Future Frontiers: AI, Genomics, and National SCD Registry.

• Organisers:

1. Department of Medicine (Cardiology), Aga Khan University Hospital.
2. Cardiac Sciences Collaboration.

• Friday (Pre-Conf & Inaugural): 08:30 AM – 09:00 PM
• Saturday (Conference): 09:00 AM – 06:00 PM

This talk brings together findings from the World Inequality Report 2026 and insights from the recent book ‘Energy and Inequality’. It shows how today’s unequal societies fuel both resentment and climate change—and how alternative paths are possible. The talk explores concrete solutions to reduce inequality within and between countries while keeping global warming in check, offering a novel perspective on what progressive policies can achieve in the years ahead.

Lucas Chancel is Associate Professor of Economics at Sciences Po Paris and Co-Director of the World Inequality Lab, a research institution coordinating the work of over 200 researchers worldwide.

This event will be held at the Impact Hub – London Euston and will also be streamed live via Zoom.

Facilitator - Rubina Zaidi

An AKU-IED alumna with over 28 years of teaching and management experience in national and international settings. International Educational Consultant, Modern Classroom Project (USA) Virtual Mentor.

 

Introduction to the Training:

This training introduces educators to the core ideas of Building Thinking Classrooms in Mathematics, a research-based framework developed by Peter Liljedahl. It focuses on creating learning environments where students think independently, collaborate meaningfully, and engage in productive struggle. The session highlights how small, intentional shifts in classroom routines can significantly strengthen mathematical reasoning and student engagement.

Participants will explore key BTC practices such as random groupings, vertical non-permanent surfaces, and purposeful thinking tasks through videos, discussions, and hands-on activities. Designed for teachers and school leaders seeking to move beyond traditional instruction, the workshop provides a practical introduction to BTC principles and supports participants in envisioning how these strategies can begin transforming their own classrooms.

 

What You’ll Learn:

  • Understand the core principles and research foundations of Building Thinking Classrooms in mathematics.
  • Analyse traditional classroom practices and identify barriers to student thinking.
  • Apply key strategies such as random grouping, vertical non-permanent surfaces, and thinking tasks in lesson design.
  • Create learning experiences using Building Thinking Classroom practices that promote student engagement, reasoning, and mathematical discourse.

 

Who Should Attend?

This workshop is designed for classroom teachers and instructional leaders, including subject coordinators, heads of department, and academic leaders. It is suitable for educators working across primary, lower secondary, and higher secondary levels who are involved in teaching, assessment, and instructional decision-making.

EventDetail:
About the Speaker

Dr Al Karim Datoo is an interdisciplinary social scientist/educationist and a qualitative researcher who works at an intersection of sociology, anthropology, philosophy, and field of educational studies (with special focus on curriculum studies, teacher education, and critical pedagogy). He has taught in higher education contexts in the UK and Pakistan. His teaching and research interests are: STEM, Humanities, sociology of Out of School Children (marginalization), diaspora and multicultural affiliations, null and hidden curricula, Globalization and cultural identities.


About the talk

  • Who is responsible for educational judgement- humans or technology/systems?
  • If authorship and control (of knowledge) gradually migrates from humans to machines - what it does to ethical agency of education?
  • Who decides what counts as knowledge? Who controls knowledge?

Foregrounding the above questions, the seminar underscores urgency to center ‘human question’ in doing STEM education. In this respect, the speaker will offer some ‘meditations’ emerged from his collaborative work on Problem of Practice (PoP) - carried out during STEM learning program with Vanderbilt University, USA & Sukkur-IBA University.

The discussion will share generation and integration of Critical Dialogical Questions (CDQs) to invoke ethico-pedgogical agency of STEM education; informed through moral philosophy, critical pedagogy, and environmental sociology.
Title: Integrating Humanities in STEM Education
Venue: AKU IED Room 5
